name: Abdul Saboor
tagline: Full-stack engineer building AI systems and the infrastructure underneath them.

hero.kicker: Software engineer — systems, interfaces, and the glue between them.

manifesto: I build software the way good editors cut film — remove everything that doesn't serve the story. Four years shipping systems that stay up, interfaces that stay out of the way, and abstractions that earn their keep.

process.title: Interrogate
process.body: Every build starts with the question behind the ticket. I read the codebase, the metrics, and the support threads before I write a line — most expensive bugs are requirements bugs.

process.title: Prototype
process.body: A working ugly thing beats a beautiful document. I ship a thin vertical slice in days, put it in front of real users, and let the surprises arrive while they're still cheap.

process.title: Harden
process.body: Then the unglamorous work: load tests, failure injection, observability, the p99 nobody sees until it pages you. Boring in production is the whole point.

process.title: Hand off
process.body: Software isn't done until the next engineer can own it. Docs that answer why, dashboards that answer what now, and an architecture a new hire can hold in their head.

testimonials.quote: Abdul is the engineer you hand the vague, high-stakes problem to. He came back with a system that's been boring — in the best way — for two years.
testimonials.author: Sara Haddad

testimonials.quote: Rare mix: cares about the p99 and the pixel. Our conversion went up because the product finally felt fast everywhere.
testimonials.author: Tom Okafor
